newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Credit firms lift Moroccan stocks slightly.
newsitem.headline: Credit firms lift Moroccan stocks slightly.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Wednesday 0.10 percent higher, lifted by gains by credit firms, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 648.38 points from 647.75 on Tuesday.
"This a slight increase but we expect the trade to be even more cautious in August. Activity might resume in September," a broker at MSI Securities said.
Credit firms, Credor gained 10 dirhams to 790 dirhams, Eqdom Credit rose 15 dirhams to 1,115 dirhams while mortgage firm Credit Hotelier et Immobilier advanced five dirhams to 312 dirhams.

ONA group, the biggest Moroccan private conglomerate, edged down three dirhams to 812 dirhams. SNI, Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private group was up one dirham to 747 dirhams.
In the banking sector, Wafabank rose five dirhams to 830 dirhams. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur dipped five dirhams to 575 dirhams.
Second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in May 1996, jumped 15 dirhams to 1,230 dirhams.
In the energy sector, Samir fell 2.50 dirhams to 339.50 dirhams. Mining firm Societe Metallurgique d'Imiter gained one dirham to 561 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 26.4 million dirhams from 26 million dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 106 million dirhams from 40 million dirhams. Main trade was in 50,000 ONA shares, a broker said. -- Newsroom 212-7 72 65 18
